Extras & Recipes

Source: vignettes/extras.Rmd
extras.Rmd
library(shiny)
library(shiny.mantine)

Components covered by the core-* vignettes each have their own mantine.dev/core/... page. This vignette covers what doesn’t: group-input variants that are sub-sections of an existing mantine.dev page rather than their own, two shiny.mantine-only drag-and-drop reordering components, and a handful of pure-R “recipe” buttons composed on top of Button() (the kind shown on ui.mantine.dev, not mantine.dev/core).

Group inputs

https://mantine.dev/core/checkbox/#checkboxgroup and https://mantine.dev/core/radio/#radiogroup — Checkbox()/Switch() are single booleans; for an array-valued group of them, use the dedicated CheckboxGroup()/SwitchGroup() plus their own CheckboxGroupItem()/ SwitchGroupItem() children (never the standalone Checkbox()/Switch(), which manage their own independent checked state and would conflict with the group’s):

Stack(
  CheckboxGroup(
    inputId = "fruits", label = "Pick fruits", value = character(0),
    CheckboxGroupItem(value = "apple", label = "Apple"),
    CheckboxGroupItem(value = "banana", label = "Banana")
  ),
  SwitchGroup(
    inputId = "features", label = "Enable features", value = character(0),
    SwitchGroupItem(value = "beta", label = "Beta features"),
    SwitchGroupItem(value = "telemetry", label = "Telemetry")
  )
)

# server:
observe(print(input$fruits))  # e.g. c("apple", "banana")

RadioGroup()/ChipGroup() (covered in vignette("core-inputs")) already follow this same pattern, but nest the plain Radio()/Chip() directly since those don’t have a separate checked state of their own to conflict with.

https://mantine.dev/core/checkbox/#checkboxcard — CheckboxCard()/ RadioCard() are card-styled selectable items: visually a bordered, clickable card instead of a small checkbox/radio circle, nested the same way inside CheckboxGroup()/RadioGroup():

RadioGroup(
  inputId = "plan", label = "Choose a plan", value = "free",
  RadioCard(value = "free", Text("Free")),
  RadioCard(value = "pro", Text("Pro"))
)

RadioIndicator()/CheckboxIndicator() are the purely decorative “checked” look Radio()/Checkbox() render internally, usable without a real input behind them — e.g. a read-only status list:

Group(RadioIndicator(checked = TRUE), Text("Step 1 complete"))

Drag-and-drop reordering (shiny.mantine extras)

Not mantine.dev components — built on @hello-pangea/dnd to fill a gap Mantine core itself doesn’t cover. After each reorder, input[[inputId]] receives the new order as a vector of value.

SortableList() reorders a plain list of list(value=, label=) items, optionally restricting the drag start to a handle icon:

SortableList(
  "elements", withHandle = TRUE,
  items = list(
    list(value = "H", label = "Hydrogen"),
    list(value = "He", label = "Helium")
  )
)

# server:
observe(print(input$elements))  # e.g. c("He", "H") after dragging Helium to the top

SortableTable() is the same idea for full table rows (cells = the values for each column):

SortableTable(
  "periodic_rows",
  columns = c("Symbol", "Name"),
  items = list(
    list(value = "H", cells = list("H", "Hydrogen")),
    list(value = "He", cells = list("He", "Helium"))
  )
)

Button recipes

Pure R compositions on top of Button()/ActionIcon() for patterns shown on ui.mantine.dev/category/buttons — not separate mantine.dev/core pages, so not covered in vignette("core-buttons"). See inst/examples/buttons-app.R for a runnable demo of all of them together.

ColorSchemeToggle() flips the whole MantineProvider()’s light/dark theme:

ColorSchemeToggle(inputId = "scheme_toggle")

ButtonWithMenu() opens a dropdown menu on click, items passed as menuItem():

ButtonWithMenu(
  "Create new",
  menuItem("create_action", "project", "Project"),
  menuItem("create_action", "folder", "Folder")
)

SplitButton() pairs a primary action with a small arrow opening a menu of alternatives:

SplitButton(
  "Send", inputId = "send_btn",
  menuItem("send_action", "now", "Send now"),
  menuItem("send_action", "schedule", "Schedule send")
)

LoadingProgressButton() shows a simulated progress bar over itself on click; input[[inputId]] receives TRUE when it reaches 100%:

LoadingProgressButton("Upload", inputId = "upload_done", loadingLabel = "Uploading...")

SocialButton() is a preconfigured icon + color + label for a common provider ("google", "twitter", "facebook", "github", "discord") — copy and adapt its source in R/Buttons.R if you need another provider:

Stack(
  SocialButton("google", inputId = "google_login"),
  SocialButton("github", inputId = "github_login")
)
